get_current.reason: arm64 current task: `mrs sp_el0` in EL1. The SVC boundary contract locates the same object (anchor current, SP_EL0) and binds it from live state

percpu_down_read.reason: filesystem freeze protection (sb->s_writers per-CPU rwsem); replay is sequential on one CPU and frozen superblocks are outside the admitted states
percpu_down_read.implementation: no-op ordering model: acquisition always succeeds and its counters are not entry state

percpu_up_read.reason: filesystem freeze protection (sb->s_writers per-CPU rwsem); replay is sequential on one CPU and frozen superblocks are outside the admitted states
percpu_up_read.implementation: no-op ordering model: acquisition always succeeds and its counters are not entry state

raw_atomic_read_acquire.reason: arm64 load-acquire (ldar) of v->counter; on one CPU in sequential replay it is a plain read of the counter
raw_atomic_read_acquire.implementation: reads *v; ordering has no effect in sequential replay

array_index_mask_nospec.reason: arm64 implements the Spectre index mask in assembly (cmp/sbc/csdb); its value is all-ones when index < size, else zero, as in the generic C body in include/linux/nospec.h

raw_atomic64_cmpxchg.reason: last C function before the arm64 LL/SC or LSE cmpxchg assembly; replay is sequential on one CPU with no concurrent tasks; it reads and conditionally writes v->counter

mutex_lock.reason: replay is sequential on one CPU with no concurrent tasks; uncontended mutexes always succeed; lock words are not entry state

mutex_unlock.reason: replay is sequential on one CPU with no concurrent tasks; uncontended mutexes always succeed; lock words are not entry state

rcu_read_lock.reason: replay is sequential on one CPU with no concurrent tasks; RCU read-side sections delimit no observable state and no grace period completes during one call

rcu_read_unlock.reason: replay is sequential on one CPU with no concurrent tasks; RCU read-side sections delimit no observable state and no grace period completes during one call

fput.reason: drops a file reference (fs/file_table.c, outside the current closure); a descriptor-table reference keeps the file alive, so release work is not reached
fput.implementation: reads and writes the struct file; refined when fs/file_table.c joins the closure

volatile_fields.reason: TIF_* bits may be set asynchronously by other CPUs or interrupts; replay is sequential on one CPU, so the entry value is a snapshot
volatile_fields.validated_by: live state field task.thread_info.flags captured at the SVC boundary

state_ranges.reason: small-table processes use the embedded fdtab with NR_OPEN_DEFAULT (BITS_PER_LONG) descriptors

pointer_extents.reason: alloc_fdtable/files_struct init size the descriptor array to max_fds entries
pointer_extents.validated_by: live binding reads fd[0..max_fds-1] at the SVC boundary

operand_free_asm.reason: in this kernel, asm without operands is barrier(), dmb/dsb/isb, msr daif and similar: they order or mask but access no C object; traps are recognized separately
operand_free_asm.validated_by: contract per configured kernel; asm templates are not in the Clang JSON AST

volatile_accesses.reason: READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE and rcu_dereference use volatile for single-copy atomicity; replay is sequential on one CPU with no concurrent tasks; MMIO pointers stay unresolved integer addresses
volatile_accesses.validated_by: every resolved volatile read is an entry read checked against live state
